turns.t: It's the hands again, doctor. The tingling, it's the left, no, sorry, it's the right one that's worse, but the left has joined in as well.
Go on, tell me more about the tingling.
It's mostly at night. I wake up with the pins and needles in my fingers, and I have to shake them out over the side of the bed.
Mm. And how long has it been going on this time?
Ah, let me think. Since after Christmas. About eight weeks. Or maybe nine, I lose track of the weeks since I retired.
Eight or nine weeks, and mostly at night. What about during the day?
In the morning my fingers are numb, like they're not mine. It wears off once I've had my tea. And I'm after dropping a cup twice this week, which is not like me.
Numb fingers in the morning, and dropped cups.
I broke Mary's good cup. She wasn't thrilled.
I'm sure she'll forgive you. Now, the last time you were here we tried a few things. How have they worked out?
The tablets help at night, I'd say. Better than before. The pregabalin, 75 mg, one at night. That's what I take.
Pregabalin, 75 milligrams at night. Anything else you're taking?
The vitamin B12, the tablets, 1000 micrograms. Once a day, with breakfast. Or is it with dinner? I take it with breakfast.
With breakfast is fine. And is there any pain in your neck, when you turn your head?
No neck pain. It's clear as a bell.
And the shoulders, any pain there, or down the arm?
None. Just from the elbow down.
And any rash on the hands, or on the arms?
No rash. The skin is grand.
Good. Tell me, is there anything long-term in your medical history that I should remember?
The carpal tunnel, the doctor before you called it that. And the low B12, that's why the tablets. And the arthritis in my thumb, the left one.
Carpal tunnel, low B12, and thumb arthritis. Thank you. Any allergies?
None that I know of. I've never had a reaction to anything.
All right. Let me ask about the rest of you. How's the heart, any racing or fluttering?
The heart is fine. Not a flutter.
And your stomach and bowels?
All normal. I'm regular as clockwork, you could set your watch.
Good to hear. Let me take your blood pressure while we're here.
Blood pressure is 126 over 78. And your pulse is 72.
Is that good for an old man?
It's very good for any man. Now, what's the thing you'd most like to be able to do with those hands again?
Hold a fishing rod through the night without waking. And Mary's cups, I suppose.
Then those are our targets. Keep the wrist straight when you sleep, and shake the hands out in the morning before you pick up anything hot.
I'll put a note on the kettle.
Do. Stay with the same tablets for now. I'd like to see you again in six weeks, and we'll see where things stand.
Six weeks, right. Will I remember it? I'll tell Mary to write it on the fridge.
The desk will give you a card as well.
Grand, grand. Thanks very much, doctor.
Mind yourself, and mind the cups.

chief_complaint.value: It's the hands again, doctor. The tingling

clinical_actions.description: Keep wrist straight when sleeping and shake out hands in the morning
